confirmed: Read the entire 254-line markdown conversion and all 10 PDF pages, including the concluding references; there are no appended supplements. The source is the published DESIGN 2024 conference paper from Cambridge University Press, printed pp. 2207-2216, with the title and four authors recorded in the form (PDF pp. 1 and 10; full-document review).

The paper contains one nonrandomized student comparison: students could opt for the traditional approach. No randomized people study is reported; quasi_people, observational context, and core = no are supported (PDF p. 4 / printed p. 2210, section 3.1; PDF pp. 8-9, section 6 limitations).

The reported participation/comparison sample is 21 students: 12 image GenAI and 9 traditional. These are people, not images or ratings, and are below the 50-person threshold; the paper states no exclusions or separate participant flow, and randomized counts appropriately remain null (PDF p. 4 / printed p. 2210, section 3.1; PDF p. 5, sections 4-5).

Participants were fourth-year undergraduate industrial design students making inspiration boards for self-determined capstone projects. Midjourney was the image-generation tool, its model version is not stated, and basic training was offered; traditional boards used internet or magazine image searching and collage (PDF p. 4 / printed p. 2210, sections 3.1-3.3).

Two coders scored the produced boards and their scores were averaged. The paper defines Diversity as variety within each board, on a 1 (very uniform) to 5 (very diverse) scale, supporting flexibility/with_ai rather than across_people diversity; Quantity counts distinct images within a board (PDF p. 5 / printed p. 2211, section 4).

S1-O1 reported values match the PDF table exactly: GenAI Median = 1.50, MAD = 0.23; Control Median = 4.50, MAD = 1.14; P-value = 0.0015. Section 5 identifies one-tailed T-tests and defines MAD as mean absolute deviation (PDF p. 5, section 5; PDF p. 6 / printed p. 2212, Table 1).

S1-O2 reported values match the PDF table exactly: GenAI Median = 18.50, MAD = 17.43; Control Median = 12.00, MAD = 6.89; P-value = 0.0090. These are image-count summaries per board, not participant counts (PDF p. 5, section 4; PDF p. 6 / printed p. 2212, Table 1; PDF p. 7, quantity paragraph).

The one_line_finding accurately reports the sample split, lower within-board variety, higher image quantity, medians, and one-tailed p-values as group comparisons (PDF p. 4, section 3.1; PDF pp. 5-7, section 5 and Table 1).

This is a primary empirical study, not a synthesis; leaving synthesis study counts and pooled estimates null/empty is appropriate. No supplement, preregistration, shared-sample statement, or data/code URL is stated in the document (PDF pp. 1-10, especially methods pp. 4-5 and conclusion/references pp. 9-10).
summary: This is a nonrandomized comparison of 21 students (12 Midjourney, 9 traditional), and the form's design, counts, reported statistics, and one-line finding are supported by the published PDF. Corrections are needed for omitted fidelity and ambiguity outcomes and incomplete contrast metadata.
